overview.name: spring-rest-sakila
overview.purpose: `spring-rest-sakila` implements a versioned, secured REST and hypermedia API over a modified MySQL Sakila DVD-rental database. It supports authentication, catalog browsing and maintenance, customer and staff administration, location and store management, inventory and rental lifecycle operations, payment records, and aggregate sales reporting, with build-time generation of API documentation artifacts.
overview.architecture: A single Java 17 Spring Boot application organized into 13 analyzed functional and infrastructure modules. Feature packages for auth, catalog, customer, location, payment, rental, staff, and store generally follow a controller–service–repository structure with separate DTOs, JPA entities, MapStruct mappers, QueryDSL projections, and Spring HATEOAS assemblers. `common` supplies shared domain contracts, exception translation, request correlation, JWT components, and predicate helpers; `config` wires security, persistence/query facilities, Redis caching, and logging. Persistence targets the MySQL Sakila schema, including its views, triggers, functions, and stored procedures. Security is configured as stateless: `/login` is permitted, other requests require authentication, and feature controllers declare role restrictions. Redis-backed Spring caching is configured globally, while evidenced cache use is concentrated in selected catalog reads.
technologies: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, and Spring HATEOAS
Spring Security with stateless JWT authentication and BCrypt password encoding
Spring Data JPA, Jakarta Persistence, Hibernate, and MySQL Connector/J
QueryDSL JPA, QueryDSL SQL/MySQL, and Blaze-Persistence
Spring Data Redis, Lettuce, and Spring Cache
SLF4J MDC and Spring request logging
Spring Boot Actuator and Micrometer Prometheus support
JTS geometry and WKB conversion APIs
JUnit 5, Mockito, MockMvc, Spring REST Docs, Asciidoctor, and OpenAPI/Postman generation
entry_points: `com.example.app.SpringRestSakilaApplication` is the Spring Boot executable entry point.
`com.example.app.services.auth.controller.LoginController` exposes `POST /login` and returns a JWT in a Bearer `Authorization` response header.

Resource APIs are exposed through `com.example.app.services.catalog.controller.ActorController`, `com.example.app.services.catalog.controller.FilmController`, `com.example.app.services.customer.controller.CustomerController`, `com.example.app.services.location.controller.LocationController`, `com.example.app.services.payment.controller.PaymentController`, `com.example.app.services.rental.controller.RentalController`, `com.example.app.services.staff.controller.StaffController`, and `com.example.app.services.store.controller.StoreController`.
`com.example.app.services.store.controller.ReportController` exposes category-sales and store-sales reporting operations.
`gradle build` is the principal build and verification entry point; the GitHub Actions workflow invokes it on Ubuntu with JDK 17.
`sql/sakila-schema-modified.sql` is the database-provisioning entry point for the modified Sakila schema and its views, triggers, functions, and stored procedures.
key_workflows: Authentication: `LoginController` obtains a user, creates a JWT, and delegates custom-token authentication through `com.example.app.services.auth.service.SecurityService` and Spring Security. `com.example.app.services.auth.service.JpaUserDetailsService` loads authority data by email and delegates password verification to a configured `PasswordEncoder`.

Authenticated request handling: `com.example.app.common.filter.MdcLoggingFilter` preserves or creates an `X-Request-ID` and manages MDC state, while `com.example.app.common.security.JwtAuthenticationFilter` processes requests except the exact `/login` servlet path. The security configuration requires authentication elsewhere and disables CSRF, CORS, and form login.

Resource operations: feature controllers bind HTTP requests and enforce declared roles; services establish transaction boundaries, map DTOs and entities, perform not-found handling, and delegate persistence to Spring Data repositories. HATEOAS assemblers add self, collection, and related-resource links, frequently using `@JsonUnwrapped` response wrappers.

Catalog management: actor and film services support filtering, pagination, projected detail reads, actor-film associations, and selected single-resource caching. Mutations map request DTOs into JPA entities and update or evict relevant actor or film cache entries where evidenced.

Customer, staff, location, payment, and store management: dedicated services provide CRUD-style operations and detail views, with QueryDSL used for joined projections or associated payment, rental, staff, and store data.

Rental lifecycle: `com.example.app.services.rental.service.RentalServiceImpl` coordinates inventory, customer, staff, rental, and payment components during rental creation, persists rental state, locates active unreturned rentals, and supports return operations. Overdue-amount operations remain placeholders.

Reporting: `com.example.app.services.store.service.ReportServiceImpl` runs read-only workflows and delegates category and store sales aggregation to `com.example.app.services.payment.repository.PaymentRepository`; QueryDSL projections implement the evidenced aggregate queries.

Build and documentation: tests feed Spring REST Docs snippets into Asciidoctor, with OpenAPI and Postman generation also configured as build artifacts. The supplied controller tests exercise representative actor success paths with mocked services.
overview.complexity_summary: Static metadata covers 213 files, 265 Java types, 652 methods, and 13 modules, with one parser-warning file. The listed complexity hotspots are predominantly field-by-field `equals(Object)` implementations on DTOs and entities rather than orchestration or query workflows. The maximum cyclomatic complexity is 16 in both `com.example.app.services.catalog.domain.dto.FilmDto.Film.equals` and `com.example.app.services.catalog.domain.entity.FilmEntity.equals`; `com.example.app.services.catalog.domain.dto.FilmDto.FilmRequest.equals` is 14. Other listed equality methods range from 8 to 12. Configuration, controllers, assemblers, and most service methods are described as low-complexity or straight-line, although low cyclomatic complexity does not account for cross-module coordination, persistence mappings, generated code, or database query cost.
noteworthy_aspects: The application models a broad portion of the Sakila DVD-rental domain: actors, films, categories, customers, locations, staff, stores, inventory, rentals, payments, authorities, and sales reports.
The API consistently separates HTTP representations, application services, persistence models, and hypermedia assembly. Many responses flatten wrapped DTO fields with Jackson `@JsonUnwrapped`.

QueryDSL and Blaze-Persistence support projected and filtered reads. Some extension repositories are intentionally empty or incomplete, and several single-result implementations use `Optional.of` where the query may return null.

Entity models frequently expose read-only scalar foreign-key identifiers alongside writable JPA relationships for the same columns. Mapper definitions commonly omit relationships, leaving association coordination to services or other code.

The modified Sakila schema includes reporting views, full-text film indexing maintained by triggers, and stored routines for rewards, customer balances, inventory availability, and rental-holder lookup.
Selected actor and film reads use Redis-backed Spring caching with a configured default TTL of one minute. Actor-film association changes do not visibly invalidate actor-related cache entries.

Runtime configuration contains MySQL, Redis, and JWT credentials or secrets directly in `application.yaml`; external secret storage, validation, and rotation are not evidenced. Hibernate `show-sql` is enabled.

`com.example.app.common.exception.GlobalExceptionHandler` translates selected exceptions to predefined errors but also invokes `printStackTrace()`, potentially emitting diagnostics outside the configured logging pipeline.

Role persistence uses a comma-separated scalar conversion and a database `SET` limited to `ROLE_READ`, `ROLE_WRITE`, `ROLE_MANAGE`, and `ROLE_ADMIN`. Password fields are not evidenced as excluded from generated string representations.

The build integrates tests, REST Docs, Asciidoctor, OpenAPI, and Postman generation, while the GitHub Actions workflow performs build verification only and defines no deployment or explicit artifact publication.
limitations: This overview is based on static metadata and validated summaries; it does not establish runtime behavior, deployed configuration, database contents, transaction outcomes, query plans, or external MySQL and Redis availability.
One of 213 analyzed files produced a parser warning, so findings associated with that file may be incomplete.

MapStruct implementations, Lombok-generated members, Spring Data repository implementations, framework proxies, and other generated behavior are not directly represented by the summarized source evidence.

JWT signature, expiration, and claim-validation semantics are not fully evidenced across the filter and provider summaries. No token revocation, persistence, or cache is shown, and lower-layer authorization beyond controller declarations cannot be inferred.

Several implementation gaps constrain workflows: `com.example.app.services.location.repository.custom.CustomAddressRepositoryImpl` returns null or empty placeholders; payment-detail methods in `com.example.app.services.payment.repository.custom.CustomPaymentRepositoryImpl` are stubbed; rental overdue operations are placeholders; and store-staff mutations in `com.example.app.services.store.service.StoreServiceImpl` are incomplete.

Known static defects include a null-condition dereference path in `com.example.app.services.catalog.repository.custom.CustomActorRepositoryImpl.findActorFilmById`, nullable query results passed to `Optional.of` in several custom repositories, and composite entities whose Spring Data repositories are declared with `Integer` identifier types.

The supplied tests emphasize actor-controller success paths and representative converter mappings. They do not establish broad error handling, authorization, malformed-input behavior, persistence integration, cache behavior, or exhaustive converter semantics.

Cyclomatic-complexity results emphasize source-level branching and are dominated by equality methods; they do not measure database complexity, entity-graph behavior, framework configuration risk, or cross-service coupling.

The module combines application bootstrap wiring, a modified Sakila schema with database-side reporting and inventory routines, build and documentation generation, observability configuration guidance, and continuous-build automation.

noteworthy_aspects: The configured root project name is `spring-rest-sakila`.
The documented REST API covers actors, customers, films, payments, rentals, reports, staffs, and stores, but the supplied evidence does not include their Java implementations.
The application requires an externally provisioned and populated MySQL Sakila database; example configuration uses `jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/sakila` with example `sakila` credentials.

The SQL schema persists film catalog, inventory, rental, payment, customer, staff, store, address, and authorization data. It also maintains `film_text` through triggers and provides full-text indexing.

Database views provide person listings, film/actor aggregation, and sales reports. `sales_by_film_category` may attribute one payment to multiple categories when a film has multiple category assignments.
Stored routines implement reward qualification, customer-balance calculation, inventory availability, and rental-holder lookup using typed parameters and static SQL; no dynamic SQL is visible.
The build makes Asciidoctor depend on tests and uses generated REST Docs snippets to produce documentation. OpenAPI and Postman generation are also configured as build artifacts.
Tests run on JUnit Platform with passed, failed, and skipped event logging; debug logging additionally captures streams, stack traces, and full exception formatting.
Spring Data Redis, Spring Security, JWT, QueryDSL, and Blaze Persistence are declared, but the supplied files do not establish their runtime configuration or behavior.
Documented management exposure includes health and Prometheus web endpoints and excludes all JMX endpoints.
The GitHub Actions workflow performs checkout, Zulu JDK 17 setup, Gradle setup, and `gradle build`; it does not define deployment, credential handling, or explicit artifact publication.
`processResources` includes duplicate resources rather than rejecting or excluding them.

files.summary: Creates a modified Sakila MySQL schema with authorization-linked customers and staff, rental and payment persistence, full-text film search synchronization, reporting views, and stored routines for customer rewards, balance calculation, and inventory availability.
noteworthy_aspects: This is SQL schema and database-program source, not Java source; no cataloged Java types or methods overlap the supplied chunk.
The schema persists rental-store operations: film cataloging, actor/category associations, store inventory, rentals, payments, staff, customers, geographic addresses, and authorization records.
`authority.password` uses a binary collation (`utf8mb4_bin`) and has a maximum length of 60 characters; the file does not establish how passwords are generated, hashed, or verified.
`film_text` has a full-text index over title and description. Its three triggers insert, conditionally update, or delete the corresponding search row when `film` changes.

`customer_list` and `staff_list` join people to address, city, and country. `film_list` and `nicer_but_slower_film_list` aggregate actor names by film and category. `sales_by_store` and `sales_by_film_category` aggregate payment amounts across rental relationships.
`sales_by_film_category` can attribute a film's payments to every category assigned to that film, so summing its category totals can count the same payment more than once.

`actor_info` uses a correlated subquery per actor/category grouping to construct categorized film titles, in addition to joins and `GROUP_CONCAT`; this is more query-intensive than the simpler listing views based on the visible query structure.

`rewards_report` calculates the prior calendar month, creates a temporary table of qualifying customers, sets `count_rewardees`, returns matching `customer` rows, and drops the temporary table. It emits a result message and exits when either threshold is zero. Qualifiers must be strictly greater than both supplied thresholds.

`get_customer_balance` returns rental charges plus late-day charges minus payments through an effective date. The visible late-fee query uses `return_date`; the source does not show alternative handling for rentals whose return date is null.
`film_in_stock` and `film_not_in_stock` each return matching inventory identifiers as a result set and place their count in an OUT parameter, relying on `inventory_in_stock`.

`inventory_held_by_customer` returns the customer for an unreturned rental of an inventory item, or null when its `NOT FOUND` handler is invoked. The source does not constrain the query to one rental row.

`inventory_in_stock` considers inventory in stock when it has no rentals or no rental with a null `return_date`; it performs a rental count followed, when necessary, by a left-join count of unreturned rentals.
